intro: Welcome to C1! Formal English has a special verb form for rules and recommendations: It is essential that every employee be on time, I suggest that she attend the briefing. Today you'll learn this form (the subjunctive), the formal were (If I were…, as it were) and the politest way to offer help in an email: Should you need any help, please call me.
teachingNotes: Recap in one line, don't re-teach: from b1-second-conditional the learner knows If I were you, I'd … (were for every person, unreal), and from b2-wish-regrets I wish I were taller. In b2-formal-writing they met the phrase 'It is also recommended that staff receive a certificate' (receive, not receives): use it as the hook. New idea (objective mandative-subjunctive): after words of requirement or necessity (essential, vital, important, crucial, necessary, imperative; require, ask) + that, formal English uses the subjunctive = the BASE FORM for every person: no -s, no -ed, no to (It is essential that he be on time; It is vital that each department submit its budget by Friday). be stays be for every person. Negative = not + base form, no do (that he not be late). Passive = be + third form (that all forms be signed). It does not change after a past main verb (It was essential that he be there). Explain 'subjunctive' in plain Indonesian: bentuk dasar kata kerja, tanpa -s/-ed/to, untuk tuntutan, syarat atau saran resmi.

Be honest about variation: the base form is standard in American English and in formal writing everywhere. British English also uses should + base form (that he should attend: formal, correct) and, in everyday speech, the normal present (that he attends). Accept all three in free answers and never mark should + base form as an error. Only treat clear errors as wrong: that he will be, that he to attend, that he being. Adding must (that he must be) is redundant and sounds wrong to most speakers: advise against it. In checkpoint gaps that explicitly ask for the subjunctive, 'is / attends' gets partial credit with this explanation. Less formal alternatives: It's important for him to be on time; He must be on time. Indonesian trap: 'Penting agar/supaya dia ...' has no tense, so learners add will (it feels like the future) or to (from 'untuk'), or must (from 'harus').

Objective suggest-recommend-that: suggest / recommend / insist / demand / propose / request (that) + person + base form (I suggest (that) she attend the briefing; Bu Ani insisted that the report be sent today; The manager suggested that Rina lead the project: lead, not led). No person -> suggest / recommend + -ing (I suggest leaving early). British also: I suggest that she should attend, I suggest she attends (informal): both accepted. The node's main error, from 'menyarankan dia untuk': *'I suggest her to attend' -> I suggest (that) she attend. Also *'I suggest to leave early' -> I suggest leaving early. Explain the contrast: advise / ask / tell / encourage DO take person + to (I advised her to attend); suggest doesn't. recommend + person + to appears in some British dictionaries but is less common: don't teach it, don't penalise it heavily. Meaning change: when insist / suggest report a fact or claim, use normal tenses (He insisted that he was innocent; The data suggests that sales are falling). insist on + -ing is a phrase to remember.

Objective were-and-formal-should, part 1: were for every person in unreal situations, preferred in formal writing (If the manager were less busy, he would reply himself; If it were up to me, …); was is common in everyday speech (accept it in speaking, prefer were in formal writing). as it were = so to speak (kalau boleh dibilang, ibaratnya): it flags a figure of speech; it is NOT 'as it was' (normal past, 'apa adanya'). were it not for + noun (= if it weren't for, kalau bukan karena) is a phrase to remember only. Do not teach inversion (Had I known, Were I to …, Not only …, Never have I …): it has its own lesson. Fixed old phrases with the base form may be named for reading only: Be that as it may, if need be, so be it, God bless you, Long live …

Objective were-and-formal-should, part 2: formal should for polite offers and conditions: Should + subject + base form = If (formal, polite, a little distant, the situation is possible but not very likely). Should you need any help, please call me (= If you need …). Should you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact us. Should the flight be delayed, we will inform you by SMS. Should there be any changes, … The node's error: *'Should you needed any help' -> Should you need. Also *'Should you to need', *'If should you need'. Trap: should here does not mean 'seharusnya / harus': it means 'apabila'. Teach it as a pattern (it is technically an inversion; the inversion lesson comes later). Contexts: HR emails, hotel and airline messages, university regulations, invented ministry circulars.

Limits: all A0-B2 grammar is known (conditionals, wish, passive in all tenses, participle clauses, formal vocabulary). Don't teach other C1 structures: cleft sentences, nominalisation, impersonal passives beyond the known phrase 'It is recommended that …', full inversion. At C1 many choices are style and register: say so, and only test clear cases. Keep examples adult and Indonesian: offices, HR, campuses, ministries, NGOs, hotels, rupiah.

keyPoints.title: Requirements: It is essential that he be …
keyPoints.explanation: After words of necessity (essential, vital, important, crucial, necessary, require) + that, formal English uses the subjunctive: the base form of the verb for every person, with no -s, no -ed and no to. be stays be. Negative: not + base form (that he not be late). Passive: be + third form (that all forms be signed). British English also says that he should attend or, informally, that he attends. Wrong: that he will be, that he to be.

examples.en: It is essential that he be on time for the audit.
examples.id: Dia wajib datang tepat waktu untuk audit.

examples.en: It is vital that each department submit its budget by Friday.
examples.id: Setiap departemen wajib menyerahkan anggarannya paling lambat hari Jumat.

examples.en: It is important that the speaker not be interrupted.

id.title: Syarat: It is essential that he be …
id.explanation: Setelah kata-kata yang menyatakan keharusan (essential, vital, important, crucial, necessary, require) + that, bahasa Inggris formal memakai subjunctive: bentuk dasar kata kerja untuk semua orang, tanpa -s, tanpa -ed dan tanpa to. be tetap be. Negatif: not + bentuk dasar (that he not be late). Pasif: be + bentuk ketiga (that all forms be signed). Bahasa Inggris Britania juga memakai that he should attend atau, dalam bahasa santai, that he attends. Yang salah: that he will be, that he to be.

keyPoints.title: suggest / recommend / insist (that) + base form
keyPoints.explanation: Verbs that ask for something (suggest, recommend, insist, demand, propose, request) take (that) + person + base form: I suggest (that) she attend the briefing. The base form stays after a past verb: He suggested that Rina lead the project. With no person, use -ing: I suggest leaving early. British English also accepts I suggest she attends (informal). The clear mistake is suggest + person + to: 'I suggest her to attend'.

examples.en: I suggest (that) she attend the briefing.
Our auditors recommend that the company change its password policy.
examples.id: Auditor kami menyarankan agar perusahaan mengubah kebijakan kata sandinya.

examples.en: I suggest leaving before the rush hour.
examples.id: Saya sarankan berangkat sebelum jam sibuk.

id.title: suggest / recommend / insist (that) + bentuk dasar
id.explanation: Kata kerja yang meminta sesuatu (suggest, recommend, insist, demand, propose, request) diikuti (that) + orang + bentuk dasar: I suggest (that) she attend the briefing. Bentuk dasarnya tetap walaupun kata kerja utamanya past: He suggested that Rina lead the project. Kalau tanpa orang, pakai -ing: I suggest leaving early. Bahasa Inggris Britania juga menerima I suggest she attends (santai). Kesalahan yang jelas adalah suggest + orang + to: 'I suggest her to attend'.

keyPoints.title: The formal were and Should you …
keyPoints.explanation: were is the subjunctive for unreal situations, for every person, and formal writing prefers it to was: If I were in your position, I would accept. Fixed phrases: as it were (= so to speak) and were it not for (= if it weren't for). For a formal, polite offer, start with Should + subject + base form (= If): Should you need any help, please call me. Not 'Should you needed'. Here should means 'if', not 'must'.

examples.en: If I were in your position, I would accept the offer.
examples.id: Kalau saya di posisimu, saya akan menerima tawaran itu.

examples.en: She is, as it were, the bridge between the two departments.
examples.id: Dia, ibaratnya, jembatan antara kedua departemen itu.

examples.en: Should you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact us.
examples.id: Apabila Anda memiliki pertanyaan, jangan ragu menghubungi kami.

id.title: were formal dan Should you …
id.explanation: were adalah subjunctive untuk situasi yang tidak nyata, untuk semua orang, dan tulisan formal lebih memilihnya daripada was: If I were in your position, I would accept. Frasa tetap: as it were (= kalau boleh dibilang) dan were it not for (= kalau bukan karena). Untuk tawaran yang formal dan sopan, mulai dengan Should + subjek + bentuk dasar (= If): Should you need any help, please call me. Bukan 'Should you needed'. Di sini should berarti 'apabila', bukan 'harus'.

guidedPractice.prompt: A university regulation about final theses. Complete with the subjunctive of the verb in brackets: It is necessary that every thesis ___ (include) a signed declaration of originality.
expected: include
should include
guidedPractice.hint: After necessary that, use the base form for every subject: no -s, even after every thesis.

guidedPractice.prompt: A company IT policy. Complete with the subjunctive of the verb in brackets: It is crucial that staff ___ (not / leave) their laptops unlocked in the office.
expected: not leave
should not leave
shouldn't leave
guidedPractice.hint: Negative subjunctive: not + base form, with no do or don't.

guidedPractice.prompt: Correct the mistake: Rina's mentor suggested her to apply for the scholarship in Australia.
expected: rina's mentor suggested that she apply for the scholarship in australia
rina's mentor suggested she apply for the scholarship in australia
rina's mentor suggested that she should apply for the scholarship in australia
rina's mentor suggested applying for the scholarship in australia
guidedPractice.hint: suggest never takes person + to. Use suggest (that) + she + base form (or should + base form).

guidedPractice.prompt: Your team is tired after a three-hour meeting. Complete with suggest and the verb in brackets: I ___ (take) a short break.
expected: suggest taking
guidedPractice.hint: There's no person after suggest, so use suggest + -ing.

guidedPractice.prompt: Make this line from an email more formal. Start with Should: If you have any questions, please contact Bu Ani in the HR office.
expected: should you have any questions please contact bu ani in the hr office
guidedPractice.hint: Should + you + base form replaces If you … The rest of the sentence stays the same.

independentPractice.prompt: Write one rule for your office, campus or building with It is essential / vital / important that … + the base form.
expected: it is essential that every visitor sign in at reception
it is vital that all staff wear their id cards
it is important that students not use their phones in the library
independentPractice.hint: It is essential that + person + base form (no -s, no will, no to).

independentPractice.prompt: A colleague wants to improve her English for an international project. Write one piece of advice with I suggest (that) she … or I recommend (that) she …
expected: i suggest that she join an online conversation class
i recommend that she read english news every day
i suggest she watch english films with subtitles
independentPractice.hint: suggest / recommend (that) + she + base form. Not 'suggest her to'.

independentPractice.prompt: You organise a seminar for an NGO in Yogyakarta. Write the last line of the formal invitation email, offering help, starting with Should you …
expected: should you need any further information please contact me
should you require accommodation please let us know
should you have any questions please do not hesitate to contact us
independentPractice.hint: Should + you + base form (need, have, require), then please …

assessment.prompt: University exam regulations. Complete with the subjunctive (the base form) of the verb in brackets: 'It is essential that every candidate ___ (be) in the examination room by 7.45 a.m.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: be (the subjunctive: the base form after essential that, the same for every person). 'should be' is also correct (formal British English). 'is' = 50 (the normal present is heard in informal British English, but the item asks for the subjunctive, and a regulation uses the formal form). 'must be' = 20 (essential already means it's necessary). 'will be' / 'to be' / 'being' = 0.

assessment.prompt: A ministry circular (an official letter) to schools about student records. Complete with the subjunctive of the verb in brackets: 'It is vital that students' personal data ___ (not / share) with any third party.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: not be shared (negative subjunctive = not + base form; passive = be + third form). 'should not be shared' is also correct. 'is not shared' = 50 (normal present: possible in informal British English, but the item asks for the subjunctive). 'not be share' = 50 (after be, the third form: shared). 'not shared' = 40 (the passive needs be). 'will not be shared' = 20. 'doesn't be shared' / 'not to share' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake in this email from a project manager in Jakarta: 'Our consultant suggested us to postpone the launch until March.'
acceptableAnswers: our consultant suggested that we postpone the launch until march
our consultant suggested we postpone the launch until march
our consultant suggested that we should postpone the launch until march
our consultant suggested we should postpone the launch until march
our consultant suggested postponing the launch until march
suggested that we postpone the launch until march
suggested we postpone the launch until march
suggested postponing the launch until march
assessment.rubric: Correct: Our consultant suggested (that) we postpone the launch until March (suggest + (that) + person + base form; the base form doesn't change after the past suggested), or suggested that we should postpone, or suggested postponing. 'suggested that we postponed' = 80 (possible in British English, but less formal). 'suggested us postponing' = 40. 'suggested to postpone' = 20. Keeping 'suggested us to postpone' = 0.

assessment.prompt: An HR email about a new leadership workshop. Complete with the subjunctive (the base form) of the verb in brackets: 'We strongly recommend that every team leader ___ (attend) the workshop on 12 November.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: attend (recommend that + base form, no -s even after every team leader). 'should attend' is also correct (British). 'attends' = 50 (possible in informal British English, but the item asks for the subjunctive used in HR documents). 'attending' = 20. 'to attend' / 'will attend' = 0.

assessment.prompt: The CEO is in Singapore, and her assistant is answering journalists' questions at a press conference in Jakarta. Complete the assistant's formal answer with the correct form of be: 'If she ___ here, she would explain the decision herself.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: were (an unreal situation: she isn't here; formal language uses were for every person). 'was' = 60 (common in everyday speech, but a formal answer uses were). 'is' = 10 (doesn't match would). 'will be' / 'would be' = 0.

assessment.prompt: At an NGO's tenth anniversary dinner in Yogyakarta, the director says: 'Our volunteers are, as it ___, the heart of this organisation.' Complete the fixed phrase.
assessment.rubric: Correct: were (as it were = so to speak, kalau boleh dibilang: it shows that 'the heart' is an image). 'was' = 10 (as it was is the normal past, 'as things were', and changes the meaning). 'is' / 'be' = 0.

assessment.prompt: The end of an email from a hotel in Bandung. Complete with the verb in brackets: 'Should you ___ (need) an airport transfer, please let us know 24 hours in advance.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: need (Should + you + base form = If you need, a formal, polite offer). 'needed' = 0 (the classic mistake: after should, always the base form). 'needs' / 'to need' / 'will need' = 0.

material.title: Rules and requirements: that he be on time

blocks.text:
**Quick recap:** you already know a special form with **were** for unreal things: *If I **were** you, I'd ask her* (B1) and *I wish I **were** taller* (B2). Formal English has one more special form, for **rules and requirements**: the **subjunctive**.

**What is it?** In this lesson, the **subjunctive** is simply the **base form** of the verb (the dictionary form: *be, attend, complete*), with **no -s, no -ed and no to**, even after *he, she, it*. It comes in a *that*-part after words that say something is **necessary** or **demanded**: **essential, vital, important, crucial, necessary, imperative** (= absolutely necessary), and the verb **require**:
- *It is **essential** that he **be** on time.* (not *is*)
- *It is **vital** that each department **submit** its budget by Friday.* (not *submits*)
- *The university **requires** that each student **submit** the form online.*

Three details:
- **be** stays **be** for every person: *that I be, that he be, that they be*.
- **Negative** = **not** + base form, with no *do*: *It is important that he **not be** late.*
- **Passive** = **be** + third form: *It is essential that all forms **be signed**.*

In B2 formal writing you met the phrase *It is also recommended that staff **receive** a certificate.* Now you know why it's *receive* and not *receives*.

id.text:
**Ulasan singkat:** kamu sudah kenal bentuk khusus **were** untuk hal yang tidak nyata: *If I **were** you, I'd ask her* (B1) dan *I wish I **were** taller* (B2). Bahasa Inggris formal punya satu bentuk khusus lagi, untuk **aturan dan syarat**: **subjunctive**.

**Apa itu?** Di pelajaran ini, **subjunctive** artinya cukup **bentuk dasar** kata kerja (bentuk di kamus: *be, attend, complete*), **tanpa -s, tanpa -ed dan tanpa to**, bahkan setelah *he, she, it*. Bentuk ini muncul di bagian *that* setelah kata-kata yang menyatakan sesuatu **harus** atau **dituntut**: **essential, vital, important, crucial, necessary, imperative** (= mutlak perlu), dan kata kerja **require** (mewajibkan):
- *It is **essential** that he **be** on time.* (bukan *is*)
- *It is **vital** that each department **submit** its budget by Friday.* (bukan *submits*)
- *The university **requires** that each student **submit** the form online.*

Tiga detail:
- **be** tetap **be** untuk semua orang: *that I be, that he be, that they be*.
- **Negatif** = **not** + bentuk dasar, tanpa *do*: *It is important that he **not be** late.*
- **Pasif** = **be** + bentuk ketiga: *It is essential that all forms **be signed**.*

Di pelajaran B2 menulis formal kamu sudah bertemu frasa *It is also recommended that staff **receive** a certificate.* Sekarang kamu tahu kenapa *receive*, bukan *receives*.

blocks.text:
**Why does 'he be' look wrong?** Normally *he* takes *is* or a verb with *-s*. But here the verb doesn't describe a fact: it describes what **must happen**. So English uses the bare base form, with no tense. That's also why it doesn't change in the past: *It **was** essential that he **be** there.*
**British vs American:** the base form is standard in American English and in formal writing everywhere. British English also uses **should + base form** (*It is essential that he **should attend***: also formal and correct) and, in everyday speech, the normal present (*It's important that he **attends***). All three are correct. What is **wrong**: *that he **will** be* ✗, *that he **to** attend* ✗.
**The Indonesian trap:** *Penting **agar** dia datang tepat waktu*. *agar / supaya* feels like the future or like *untuk*, so learners write 'that he **will be**' ✗ or 'that he **to be**' ✗. And don't add *must* (*harus*): *essential* already says it's necessary.

id.text:
**Kenapa 'he be' kelihatan salah?** Biasanya *he* memakai *is* atau kata kerja ber-*s*. Tapi di sini kata kerjanya tidak menggambarkan fakta: ia menggambarkan apa yang **harus terjadi**. Jadi bahasa Inggris memakai bentuk dasar polos, tanpa tense. Itu juga sebabnya bentuknya tidak berubah di masa lalu: *It **was** essential that he **be** there.*
**Britania vs Amerika:** bentuk dasar adalah bentuk standar dalam bahasa Inggris Amerika dan dalam tulisan formal di mana pun. Bahasa Inggris Britania juga memakai **should + bentuk dasar** (*It is essential that he **should attend***: juga formal dan benar) dan, dalam percakapan sehari-hari, present biasa (*It's important that he **attends***). Ketiganya benar. Yang **salah**: *that he **will** be* ✗, *that he **to** attend* ✗.
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** *Penting **agar** dia datang tepat waktu*. *agar / supaya* terasa seperti masa depan atau seperti *untuk*, jadi pelajar menulis 'that he **will be**' ✗ atau 'that he **to be**' ✗. Dan jangan tambahkan *must* (*harus*): *essential* sudah berarti wajib.

rows.en: It is essential that every visitor wear a helmet on the construction site.
rows.id: Setiap tamu wajib memakai helm di lokasi proyek.

rows.en: The ministry requires that each school submit its data by 30 June.
rows.id: Kementerian mewajibkan setiap sekolah menyerahkan datanya paling lambat 30 Juni.

rows.en: It is vital that the new payroll system be tested before January.
rows.id: Sistem penggajian yang baru harus diuji sebelum Januari.

rows.en: It is important that the speaker not be interrupted.
rows.note: negative: not + base form, no doesn't

id.note: negatif: not + bentuk dasar, tanpa doesn't

rows.en: It's important for him to be on time.
rows.id: Penting baginya untuk datang tepat waktu.

blocks.prompt: University library rules: It is necessary that each student ___ any library fines before graduation.
blocks.explain: After **necessary that**, formal English uses the subjunctive: the **base form** (*pay*), with no -s even after *each student*. *will* and *to* are never used in this pattern.

id.prompt: Peraturan perpustakaan kampus. Lengkapi: It is necessary that each student ___ any library fines before graduation.
id.explain: Setelah **necessary that**, bahasa Inggris formal memakai subjunctive: **bentuk dasar** (*pay*), tanpa -s walaupun subjeknya *each student*. *will* dan *to* tidak pernah dipakai dalam pola ini.

id.title: Aturan dan syarat: that he be on time

blocks.text:
The same base form comes after **verbs** that ask for something: **suggest, recommend, insist, demand, propose, request**:
- *I **suggest** (that) she **attend** the briefing.*
- *We **recommend** (that) every applicant **submit** the form online.*
- *Bu Ani **insisted** that the report **be** sent today.*
- *The union **demanded** that the company **raise** salaries.*
*that* is often left out after *suggest* and *recommend*, especially in speech.

**No person? Use -ing:** *I **suggest leaving** early.* *We **recommend booking** in advance.* (= anyone, in general)

**A past verb, the same base form:** *The manager **suggested** that Rina **lead** the project.* (not *led*: the base form has no tense.)

**British English** also says *I suggest that she **should** attend* and, informally, *I suggest she **attends***. Both are fine. **The clear mistake** is **suggest + person + to**: 'I suggest **her to attend**' ✗.

id.text:
Bentuk dasar yang sama muncul setelah **kata kerja** yang meminta sesuatu: **suggest** (menyarankan), **recommend** (menganjurkan), **insist** (bersikeras, menuntut), **demand** (menuntut), **propose** (mengusulkan), **request** (meminta secara resmi):
- *I **suggest** (that) she **attend** the briefing.*
- *We **recommend** (that) every applicant **submit** the form online.*
- *Bu Ani **insisted** that the report **be** sent today.*
- *The union **demanded** that the company **raise** salaries.*
*that* sering dihilangkan setelah *suggest* dan *recommend*, terutama dalam percakapan.

**Tidak ada orangnya? Pakai -ing:** *I **suggest leaving** early.* *We **recommend booking** in advance.* (= siapa saja, secara umum)

**Kata kerja utamanya past, bentuk dasarnya tetap:** *The manager **suggested** that Rina **lead** the project.* (bukan *led*: bentuk dasar tidak punya tense.)

**Bahasa Inggris Britania** juga memakai *I suggest that she **should** attend* dan, dalam bahasa santai, *I suggest she **attends***. Keduanya boleh. **Kesalahan yang jelas** adalah **suggest + orang + to**: 'I suggest **her to attend**' ✗.

blocks.text:
**The Indonesian trap:** *Saya **menyarankan dia untuk** ikut* → word for word 'I suggest **her to** attend' ✗. **suggest** never takes person + *to*. Say **I suggest (that) she attend** ✓ or **I suggest she attends** ✓ (British, informal). Also 'I suggest **to leave** early' ✗ → **I suggest leaving early** ✓.
**Then why is *advise her to* correct?** Some verbs (*advise, ask, tell, encourage, want*) do take person + *to*: *I advised her **to attend***. *suggest* just isn't one of them: it's a pattern to remember. With *recommend*, use *that* + base form or *-ing* too (*recommend you to* appears in some British dictionaries, but it's much less common).
**Same verb, different meaning:** when *insist* or *suggest* reports a **fact** or a **claim**, not a demand, use normal tenses: *He insisted that he **was** innocent.* (= *bersikeras bahwa*) *The data suggests that sales **are** falling.* (= *menunjukkan*)

id.text:
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** *Saya **menyarankan dia untuk** ikut* → kata per kata jadi 'I suggest **her to** attend' ✗. **suggest** tidak pernah diikuti orang + *to*. Katakan **I suggest (that) she attend** ✓ atau **I suggest she attends** ✓ (Britania, santai). Juga 'I suggest **to leave** early' ✗ → **I suggest leaving early** ✓.
**Lalu kenapa *advise her to* benar?** Beberapa kata kerja (*advise, ask, tell, encourage, want*) memang diikuti orang + *to*: *I advised her **to attend***. *suggest* bukan salah satunya: ini pola yang perlu diingat. Dengan *recommend*, pakai juga *that* + bentuk dasar atau *-ing* (*recommend you to* ada di beberapa kamus Britania, tapi jauh lebih jarang).
**Kata kerja sama, arti berbeda:** kalau *insist* atau *suggest* melaporkan **fakta** atau **klaim**, bukan tuntutan, pakai tense biasa: *He insisted that he **was** innocent.* (= *bersikeras bahwa*) *The data suggests that sales **are** falling.* (= *menunjukkan*)

rows.en: Our auditors recommend that the company change its password policy.
rows.id: Auditor kami menyarankan agar perusahaan mengubah kebijakan kata sandinya.

rows.en: Dr. Wulan insisted that every student be present at the thesis defence.
rows.id: Dr. Wulan menuntut agar setiap mahasiswa hadir di sidang skripsi.

rows.en: The committee proposed that the deadline be extended.
rows.id: Panitia mengusulkan agar tenggat waktunya diperpanjang.

rows.en: I suggest leaving before the rush hour.
rows.id: Saya sarankan berangkat sebelum jam sibuk.

rows.en: He insisted that he had sent the email.
rows.id: Dia bersikeras bahwa dia sudah mengirim email itu.
rows.note: a claim, not a demand → normal tense

blocks.prompt: A manager writes to HR about a new employee, Sari. Which sentence is correct?
options: I suggest Sari to join the mentoring programme.
I suggest that Sari join the mentoring programme.
blocks.explain: **suggest (that) + person + base form**: *that Sari join*. *suggest* never takes person + *to*, so 'suggest Sari **to** join' is wrong, even though Indonesian says *menyarankan Sari untuk*.

id.prompt: Seorang manajer menulis ke HR tentang karyawan baru, Sari. Kalimat mana yang benar?
id.explain: **suggest (that) + orang + bentuk dasar**: *that Sari join*. *suggest* tidak pernah diikuti orang + *to*, jadi 'suggest Sari **to** join' salah, walaupun dalam bahasa Indonesia kita bilang *menyarankan Sari untuk*.

material.title: The formal were: If I were…, as it were

blocks.text:
**were** is the other subjunctive form. You know it from **unreal** situations: *If I **were** you, I'd talk to her.* *I wish I **were** taller.* With *I, he, she, it*, everyday speech often says **was**, but formal writing and careful speech use **were**:
- *If the manager **were** less busy, he would reply to every email himself.* (he is busy)
- *If it **were** up to me, we would hire her.* (it isn't my decision)

Two formal phrases with **were**:
- **as it were** = *kalau boleh dibilang, ibaratnya*. It warns the listener that your words are an image, not literal: *Our IT team is, **as it were**, the engine room of the company.*
- **were it not for** + noun = *if it weren't for* = *kalau bukan karena*: ***Were it not for** the government subsidy, many small farmers could not survive.* Learn it as a **phrase to remember**: its word order (*were* before *it*) is an **inversion**, which has its own lesson later.

id.text:
**were** adalah bentuk subjunctive yang lain. Kamu sudah mengenalnya dari situasi yang **tidak nyata**: *If I **were** you, I'd talk to her.* *I wish I **were** taller.* Dengan *I, he, she, it*, percakapan sehari-hari sering memakai **was**, tapi tulisan formal dan bahasa yang cermat memakai **were**:
- *If the manager **were** less busy, he would reply to every email himself.* (kenyataannya dia sibuk)
- *If it **were** up to me, we would hire her.* (kenyataannya bukan saya yang memutuskan)

Dua frasa formal dengan **were**:
- **as it were** = *kalau boleh dibilang, ibaratnya*. Frasa ini memberi tanda bahwa kata-katamu adalah kiasan, bukan arti harfiah: *Our IT team is, **as it were**, the engine room of the company.*
- **were it not for** + kata benda = *if it weren't for* = *kalau bukan karena*: ***Were it not for** the government subsidy, many small farmers could not survive.* Hafalkan sebagai **frasa tetap**: susunan katanya (*were* sebelum *it*) adalah **inversi**, yang punya pelajarannya sendiri nanti.

blocks.text:
**as it were ≠ as it was.** *as it was* is the normal past: *I left the room as it was* (= *apa adanya*). *as it were* is a fixed phrase that softens an image; it isn't about the past at all, which is why the *were* after *it* looks 'wrong'.
**More old fixed phrases with the base form** (you'll meet them in reading; just remember them): *Be that as it may* (= *meskipun demikian*), *if need be* (= *kalau perlu*), *so be it* (= *ya sudah, biarlah*), *God bless you*, *Long live …* (= *hidup …!*).

id.text:
**as it were ≠ as it was.** *as it was* adalah past biasa: *I left the room as it was* (= *apa adanya*). *as it were* adalah frasa tetap yang memperhalus kiasan; frasa ini sama sekali tidak membicarakan masa lalu, itu sebabnya *were* setelah *it* kelihatan 'salah'.
**Frasa tetap lama lainnya dengan bentuk dasar** (akan kamu temui saat membaca; cukup diingat): *Be that as it may* (= *meskipun demikian*), *if need be* (= *kalau perlu*), *so be it* (= *ya sudah, biarlah*), *God bless you*, *Long live …* (= *hidup …!*).

blocks.prompt: A formal report: If the budget ___ larger, the NGO could open a second office in Surabaya.
blocks.explain: The budget isn't larger: it's **unreal**, and *could* shows an imagined result. So the formal subjunctive **were** (for every person). *will be* and *is being* talk about real situations and don't fit with *could*.

id.prompt: Sebuah laporan formal. Lengkapi: If the budget ___ larger, the NGO could open a second office in Surabaya.
id.explain: Anggarannya tidak lebih besar: situasinya **tidak nyata**, dan *could* menunjukkan hasil yang dibayangkan. Jadi pakai subjunctive formal **were** (untuk semua orang). *will be* dan *is being* membicarakan situasi nyata dan tidak cocok dengan *could*.

material.title: Polite offers: Should you need any help…

blocks.text:
Formal emails, letters and notices often end with a polite offer. You can write it with **if**: *If you need any help, please call me.* A more formal way starts with **Should**:
- ***Should you need** any help, please call me.* (= If you need any help …)
- ***Should you have** any questions, please do not hesitate to contact us.*
- ***Should the flight be** delayed, we will inform you by SMS.*

The pattern: **Should + subject + base form**, then the main sentence (often *please …* or *we will …*). It sounds polite and a little distant, and it suggests the situation is possible but not very likely, so it's perfect for HR emails, hotel and airline messages and official circulars.

In B2 you ended formal emails with *Thank you for your time. I look forward to hearing from you.* A *Should you …* line fits just before that. Its word order (*should* before *you*) is a kind of **inversion**; you'll learn the others later. Here, just learn **Should you …** as a pattern.

id.text:
Email, surat dan pengumuman formal sering diakhiri dengan tawaran yang sopan. Kamu bisa menulisnya dengan **if**: *If you need any help, please call me.* Cara yang lebih formal dimulai dengan **Should**:
- ***Should you need** any help, please call me.* (= If you need any help …)
- ***Should you have** any questions, please do not hesitate to contact us.*
- ***Should the flight be** delayed, we will inform you by SMS.*

Polanya: **Should + subjek + bentuk dasar**, lalu kalimat utamanya (sering *please …* atau *we will …*). Terdengar sopan dan agak berjarak, dan menyiratkan bahwa situasinya mungkin terjadi tapi tidak terlalu besar kemungkinannya, jadi pas untuk email HR, pesan dari hotel dan maskapai, serta surat edaran resmi.

Di B2 kamu menutup email formal dengan *Thank you for your time. I look forward to hearing from you.* Kalimat *Should you …* cocok diletakkan tepat sebelumnya. Susunan katanya (*should* sebelum *you*) adalah salah satu jenis **inversi**; jenis yang lain akan kamu pelajari nanti. Di sini, cukup pelajari **Should you …** sebagai pola.

blocks.text:
**The Indonesian trap:** *should* usually means *seharusnya*, but here it means ***apabila*** (formal, like *Apabila Bapak/Ibu memerlukan bantuan, …*). There's no 'must' in it.
**After Should + subject, the base form:** 'Should you **needed** any help' ✗, 'Should you **to need**' ✗, 'Should you **will need**' ✗ → **Should you need** ✓. And don't use *if* and *should* together: '**If should** you need …' ✗.

id.text:
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** *should* biasanya berarti *seharusnya*, tapi di sini artinya ***apabila*** (formal, seperti *Apabila Bapak/Ibu memerlukan bantuan, …*). Tidak ada arti 'harus' di dalamnya.
**Setelah Should + subjek, pakai bentuk dasar:** 'Should you **needed** any help' ✗, 'Should you **to need**' ✗, 'Should you **will need**' ✗ → **Should you need** ✓. Dan jangan pakai *if* dan *should* bersamaan: '**If should** you need …' ✗.

blocks.prompt: An email from a hotel in Bali. Which sentence is correct?
options: Should you wished to extend your stay, please contact the front desk.
If should you wish to extend your stay, please contact the front desk.
Should you wish to extend your stay, please contact the front desk.
blocks.explain: **Should + you + base form** (*wish*) = *If you wish*, a formal, polite offer. After *should*, never the past (*wished*), and *if* and *should* are not used together.

id.prompt: Email dari sebuah hotel di Bali. Kalimat mana yang benar?
id.explain: **Should + you + bentuk dasar** (*wish*) = *If you wish*, tawaran yang formal dan sopan. Setelah *should*, jangan pernah pakai bentuk past (*wished*), dan *if* dan *should* tidak dipakai bersamaan.

id.intro: Selamat datang di C1! Bahasa Inggris formal punya bentuk kata kerja khusus untuk aturan dan rekomendasi: It is essential that every employee be on time, I suggest that she attend the briefing. Hari ini kamu akan mempelajari bentuk ini (subjunctive), were yang formal (If I were…, as it were) dan cara paling sopan menawarkan bantuan di email: Should you need any help, please call me.

assessment.sf-1: Peraturan ujian universitas. Lengkapi dengan subjunctive (bentuk dasar) dari kata kerja dalam kurung: 'It is essential that every candidate ___ (be) in the examination room by 7.45 a.m.'
assessment.sf-2: Surat edaran kementerian (surat resmi) untuk sekolah tentang data siswa. Lengkapi dengan subjunctive dari kata kerja dalam kurung: 'It is vital that students' personal data ___ (not / share) with any third party.'
assessment.sf-3: Perbaiki kesalahan dalam email dari seorang manajer proyek di Jakarta ini: 'Our consultant suggested us to postpone the launch until March.'
assessment.sf-4: Email HR tentang workshop kepemimpinan yang baru. Lengkapi dengan subjunctive (bentuk dasar) dari kata kerja dalam kurung: 'We strongly recommend that every team leader ___ (attend) the workshop on 12 November.'
assessment.sf-5: CEO sedang di Singapura, dan asistennya menjawab pertanyaan wartawan di sebuah konferensi pers di Jakarta. Lengkapi jawaban formal asisten itu dengan bentuk be yang benar: 'If she ___ here, she would explain the decision herself.'
assessment.sf-6: Di makan malam ulang tahun kesepuluh sebuah LSM di Yogyakarta, direkturnya berkata: 'Our volunteers are, as it ___, the heart of this organisation.' Lengkapi frasa tetapnya.
assessment.sf-7: Akhir email dari sebuah hotel di Bandung. Lengkapi dengan kata kerja dalam kurung: 'Should you ___ (need) an airport transfer, please let us know 24 hours in advance.'
